record.paper_title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Curse of dimensionality on lp balls
record.original_question: For the same orthogonally invariant class C_tilde^2(D_d), it is known that the integration problem suffers from the curse of dimensionality for certain domains D_d having small radius, including l_p^d balls with p>=2. Does the curse of dimensionality also hold when D_d is an l_p^d ball with p<2?

evidence.quote: It is known that the integration problem for C~2(Dd) and certain Dd suffers from the curse of dimensionality. This is true if Dd has a small radius, see [48] for the best known results. For example, the curse is known if Dd is a lpd ball and p >= 2. It is not known for p balls and p < 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 1$ and let $D_d\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a compact, convex, orthogonally symmetric body (i.e. invariant under all orthogonal transformations of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that map $D_d$ to itself; here we take the natural symmetric body $D_d$ equal to a unit $\ell_p^d$-ball $B_p^d=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:\|x\|_p\le 1\}$). Consider the class
$$\widetilde C^2(D_d)=\bigl\{f\in C^2(D_d):\ \|f\|_\infty\le 1,\ \|\partial_v^2 f\|_\infty\le 1\text{ for every unit vector }v\in\mathbb{R}^d\bigr\},$$
i.e. functions on $D_d$ uniformly bounded by $1$ whose second directional derivative in every direction is also uniformly bounded by $1$.

For the integration problem
$$\mathrm{INT}_d(f)=\int_{D_d} f(x)\,dx,$$
define the worst-case error of an algorithm using $n$ function values as
$$e(n,d)=\inf_{x_1,\dots,x_n;\,\phi}\sup_{f\in\widetilde C^2(D_d)}\bigl|\mathrm{INT}_d(f)-\phi(f(x_1),\dots,f(x_n))\bigr|,$$
where the infimum is over all (adaptive) choices of nodes and all mappings $\phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$. Let $n(\varepsilon,d)$ be the minimal $n$ for which $e(n,d)\le\varepsilon$. One says the curse of dimensionality holds if there exist $\varepsilon_0>0$, $c>0$, and $\gamma>1$ such that
$$n(\varepsilon_0,d)\ge c\,\gamma^d\quad\text{for all }d\ge 1.$$

It is known that the curse of dimensionality holds when $D_d=B_p^d$ for $p\ge 2$. 

Question: Does the curse of dimensionality also hold for $\widetilde C^2(B_p^d)$ when $1\le p<2$?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works establishing the curse of dimensionality for the class of twice-differentiable orthogonally invariant functions on $\ell_p^d$-balls cover the regime $2\le p\le\infty$ (using thin-shell concentration of Guédon–Milman). No source found establishing or refuting the curse for $1\le p<2$, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The curse of dimensionality for numerical integration on general domains
status_evidence.snippet: Results obtained for volume-normalized lp^d balls in the complete regime 2 ≤ p ≤ ∞ via thin-shell concentration estimates of Guédon–Milman.
status_evidence.claim: Curse of dimensionality known for lp-balls with p≥2; case p<2 not addressed.

status_evidence.title: The Curse of Dimensionality for Numerical Integration of Smooth Functions II
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes curse of dimensionality for C^r classes on certain symmetric convex bodies of small radius.
status_evidence.claim: Prior results cover p≥2 case; p<2 left open.
